text:
sanjay: FYI we saw another small p95 latency spike on serving yesterday around 04:12 UTC, looks correlated with warm-pool depletion + sudden burst from onboarding tests :grimacing:
ops-bot: alert: cluster/gpu-pool-eu-west utilization exceeded 85% for 7m (auto-scale events suppressed due to cool-down)
liam: can you paste the query that caused the surge? rough QPS and avg seq len?
sanjay: short repro: onboarding job ramped ~3k requests/min, avg seq=512, sustained for ~6m. queue length climbed, admission started returning 429s then we fell back to smaller model variants.
maya: ah ok. we saw the same pattern last month but the warm-pool refill was too slow during the initial ramp. autoscaler cool-down + warmup latency mismatch.
raj: digging traces now. preliminary: warm-pool prealloc window=30s, instance startup (GPU ready + model load quantized)=~70-95s depending on model. so we never had preallocated instances ready when the burst hit.
eve: that implies two knobs: increase prealloc window or reduce instance startup (optimize image/model load), or apply stronger admission control to smooth bursts. cost vs latency tradeoff.
liam: we should avoid large permanent warm-pool increases — costy. propose short-term mitigation = extend prealloc window to 120s for high-risk pools + add a soft admission throttle when pool occupancy >75%.
sanjay: agreed. also consider burst token-bucket per-customer that drains into queue only if GPUs available, otherwise backpressure to clients with Retry-After.
raj: putting some numbers: current warm-pool size=8 nodes, baseline needed for steady QPS=6. burst headroom=2 nodes. if we increase to 12 nodes prealloc we get headroom for this test but cost +50% on that pool.
maya: can we do auto-windowing: detect ramp slope (requests/min delta) and proactively start warm-ups if slope > X? we have request rate metrics in prometheus already.
eve: yes, implement slope-based preallocation: if dQPS/min > 200 over 1m, trigger prealloc with target capacity = ceil(current+delta*factor). fallback to admission if prealloc not ready in 90s.
liam: what's the simplest experiment we can run? i want something low-risk to measure impact.
sanjay: plan: 1) canary on eu-west pool for 48h: set prealloc window=120s, add admission throttle at 80% util (reject->429+Retry-After 10s), enable slope detector with threshold 150 rps/min. 2) measure p95 latency, number of 429s, and cost delta.
raj: config snippet I suggest:
```
pool: eu-west-gpu
prealloc_window: 120s
warm_pool_min: 8
warm_pool_target: 12
admission_threshold_percent: 80
admission_mode: token_bucket
token_bucket_rate: 500rps
token_bucket_burst: 1000
slope_detector_threshold: 150
slope_detector_interval: 60s
```
liam: runbook notes: deploy canary at 02:00 UTC to avoid business hours, monitor p95, queue length, 429 counts. rollback if 429s > 1% of requests or cost increases > 30% vs baseline.
maya: also log metrics for model fallback events, and trace sample from falling back paths so we can detect quality regressions.
sanjay: assigning actions: raj -> implement config + alerting, maya -> add trace sampling + dashboard, liam -> run canary and monitor, eve -> postmortem template in case rollback needed. target to start canary in 8h.
deploy-bot: rollout scheduled: canary-config apply to eu-west-gpu at 1815085634 (in 8h).
ops-bot: note: remember dedicated customers on that pool - notify account-eng if risk > low.
sanjay: +1, i'll ping account-eng once canary is green. thanks all :thumbsup:
